solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not a prodigy and that's hardly unforeseen

definitions.meaning: a prodigy is a marvel, so someone who is not one is no marvel at all
a set phrase said of something entirely to be expected

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a dull child turned out ordinary, as anyone could have predicted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally denies being a marvel and idiomatically means something was only to be expected.

clue.text: For cost, provide better return than other hens

definitions.meaning: money spent or expenditure

definitions.text: provide better return than other hens
definitions.meaning: a hen that produces more eggs than the rest beats them in laying

explanation.surface: A poultry farmer weighs the expense of hens against their egg yield.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent is expenditure; read as two words, it means to produce more eggs than rivals.

clue.text: Bugbears, creating havoc in rose garden, for a start

indicators.note: havoc wrecks the order, so the letters are thrown about
the start of garden, its opening letter, is taken

explanation.surface: Pests are wreaking havoc in someone's rose garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugbears are objects of dread, and monstrous giants of folklore are frightening figures too.

clue.text: Daughter is taking lessons in conversation

parts.note: a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: A daughter is taking lessons to improve her conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Discussion and talk between people is spoken exchange, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Setter romping, trapping ball, gets award

indicators.note: the jumbled letters trap the ball shape inside them
romping suggests the letters of setter frolic about into a new order

parts.note: O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A crossword setter plays a romping ball game and wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romping' rearranges SETTER; 'trapping' holds O inside to give R-O-SETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette of ribbon is given as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: Copper in case prepared to make charges

indicators.note: the copper symbol is placed in the middle of the rearranged letters
the letters of case are prepared, that is made ready in a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman puts a case together so that he can bring charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CASE to ACSE, and 'in' puts CU inside it. 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring charges against someone is to formally blame them for an offence.

clue.text: Book finally almost complete

indicators.note: the phrase is not quite whole, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: Someone's book is at last nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase AT LAST loses its final T to 'almost complete'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of maps is a type of volume.

clue.text: Can't round on child — not I, nor you, one hears

definitions.text: not I, nor you, one hears

indicators.note: the contraction is put round the other pieces

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving four letters
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A parent can't get round a child who won't cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says a letter that is neither I nor U, which sounds like 'you': both vowels, so the answer is a non-vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: I and U are vowels, so a letter that is neither of these is of the other kind of speech sound.

clue.text: Reform, wicked woman!

definitions.meaning: to reform is to cast off wickedness
a spiteful, malicious woman

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means cast off badness; hyphenated it is a cruel, malevolent female.

clue.text: Is surprised to find sharp points on both ends

indicators.note: the two compass letters sit on either end of the word for sharp

parts.note: S is the compass point south, taken twice
tart means sharp or acidic in taste

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find a stick sharpened at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to jump or flinch with surprise or alarm.

clue.text: By which car was shut up in garage?

definitions.text: By which car was shut up in garage?

parts.words: By which car was shut up in garage?
parts.note: shut up suggests locking a car away in a garage, but it means made quiet: the exhaust device that muffles engine noise

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a car came to be locked away in the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler fitted to an exhaust quietens the engine, so it shuts the car up.

clue.text: Golf, according to Tiger Woods's child, is the open sesame

parts.note: to his child Tiger Woods is Pa, so golf would be described as Pa's
golf is a sport

explanation.surface: A child of the famous golfer explains what golf means to the family: the key to everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf is the father's game, so his child would call it Pa's sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is the key that opens borders, like the magic words that opened Ali Baba's cave.

clue.text: Pelt that's revealing?

definitions.meaning: to pelt is to rain down or throw a stream of things at someone
a person or thing that reveals or displays something, a whimsical agent noun

explanation.surface: An animal skin is asked whether it gives too much away.
explanation.definitionFit: To pelt with stones is to rain them down; one who displays something is, playfully, a displayer of it.

clue.text: Why former nun still dresses like one?

definitions.text: Why former nun still dresses like one?

parts.words: Why former nun still dresses like one?
parts.note: a nun wears a habit, so an ex-nun still in one would do so from routine rather than vocation

explanation.surface: A question about why a woman who has left her order still wears religious dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for acting from ingrained routine also reads as the power of a nun's garment.

clue.text: Washed out the 'a' coming in 'brainless'

indicators.note: the two short words come in to the middle of the word for washed out

parts.note: faded means washed out in colour

explanation.surface: A faded letter appears in the word brainless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' signals insertion; the quoted words are taken literally, not as a definition of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim-witted person is called a dolt or numbskull, someone stupid.

clue.text: Awfully fierce animal's gobbled food

indicators.note: the jumbled letters gobble up the beast word, holding it inside
awfully suggests the letters of fierce are badly mangled

parts.note: an ass is an animal; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A savage beast wolfed down its meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' gives FRICEE from the fodder, and 'gobbled' holds the beast inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew of meat in a white sauce is a dish to eat.

clue.text: Having large one. Week is disastrous. Yours, too?

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: disastrous suggests the words week is are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone writes of having a large one and a disastrous week, and asks if theirs was too.
explanation.definitionFit: The reply meaning the same goes for you is said back when someone wishes you well.

clue.text: What you get from water pistol held by nasty brat?

definitions.text: What you get from water pistol
definitions.meaning: a toy gun gives a small jet of water
an insignificant, irritating young person

explanation.surface: A child with a toy gun soaks people, and someone wonders what comes out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jet of water is literally what a toy gun gives, and the phrase is also slang for a pipsqueak.

clue.text: A pair of braces — some like a string one?

definitions.meaning: a brace is two, so two braces make a group of four
a classical ensemble of two violins, viola and cello

explanation.surface: Someone muses that braces come in pairs, rather like string.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pairs make a set of four, and a chamber group of four string players is a common ensemble.

clue.text: After being brought up, love dad? That's the stuff!

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: love is nil, a score of zero in tennis
pop is an informal name for dad

explanation.surface: A child brought up well says loving Dad is just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses NILPOP. 'the stuff' sounds like approval but means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-woven cotton cloth used for shirts is a kind of material.

clue.text: Pesters to form groups

definitions.meaning: to harass or trouble persistently
read as two words, to be collections or batches

explanation.definitionFit: Troubles assail and harass people; split in two, the word means to be groups or collections.

clue.text: Turn upside down to clean

definitions.meaning: to search a place exhaustively, ransacking it
to scrub hard with an abrasive

explanation.definitionFit: Searching thoroughly means ransacking a place, and scrubbing a pan hard cleans it.

clue.text: Conversion of a flat back into building

indicators.note: back says the word for a flat is read from its end

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or small home

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters of into are put together anew

explanation.surface: A developer turns a flat back into part of a larger building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PAD into DAP, and 'building' rearranges INTO into TION. 'into building' reads as a destination but is fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A change made to suit a new use, as a novel turned into a film, is a modification.

clue.text: Got engine right on song

definitions.meaning: adjusted a motor for best running
in harmony, at the right pitch

explanation.definitionFit: Mechanics adjust motors for performance, and instruments are set to the right pitch: both senses of adjust.

clue.text: Spotted almost four weeks after, somewhere in Italy

parts.note: pied means patchy in colour, like a magpie

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the period is dropped

parts.note: a month is roughly four weeks

explanation.surface: Someone was seen nearly a month later in an Italian location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter. Piedmont is a region of north-west Italy around Turin.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around Turin in north-west Italy is one place in that country.

clue.text: Still miss one

definitions.meaning: a woman still called Miss is unmarried
solitary, a lone item

explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried person is unattached; the word also means one alone.

clue.text: You are silly, retiring shamefaced

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of are are knocked into a daft new order
retiring means going back, so the word for shamefaced is read in reverse

parts.note: red-faced with embarrassment, so red

explanation.surface: Someone tells another they are silly and timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' gives REA from ARE; 'retiring' reverses RED to DER. The definition addresses the solver: you are reading the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The person addressing the page is someone reading it, which is the solver.

clue.text: Walking with great wobbling, carrying racket

indicators.note: carrying means the jumbled letters hold the noise word inside them
wobbling suggests the letters of great are unsteady and shift around

parts.note: a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Someone walks along unsteadily, swinging a tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbling' gives TREAG, and 'carrying' holds the noise inside. 'racket' suggests tennis but means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on or pacing along is going on foot.
